Ezemvelo Exposed (Investigation)

By: Julie Laurenz | Delivery

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
Accused of destroying wetlands, building illegally in conservation areas and blowing 70% of its budget on ridiculous salaries, Ezemvelo ZN Wildlife is accused of doing more harm than good.

Summary:
Formerly known as the Natal Parks Board, the organisation was once a celebrated environmental agency accredited with saving the white rhino from extinction. Areas of operation include the world’s biggest marine turtle breeding beaches, Coelacanth habitat and 2 world heritage sites.

But, according to high ranking insiders, the organisation is now chronically mismanaged with its parks in a shambles and its reputation in tatters.


Further information:
TTHE STORY

There are a number of cases of questionable and bizarre projects that see Ezemvelo going against its own mandate to protect the environment and conserve nature.
We will start with the most visually shocking – the destruction of the unauthorised” drainage of large section of the Balamhlanga natural wetland in the Makhatini Flats near Jozini. VISUALS: I’m going to take the presenter up and let them see it firsthand. We’ll open with this sequence.





• Balamhlanga Natural Wetland

Ezemvelo is currently helping to rip up and drain a large natural wetland near Jozini at a cost of R25 million. Conservationists and wetland experts want to know why the provincial conservation agency is helping to destroy a specially protected natural wetland.
At first Ezemvelo and the Department of Agriculture and Environmental Affairs said they were just trying to get rid of a “weed invasion”. However, wetland experts have confirmed that the bulrushes at Balamhlanga are not alien, but indigenous to South Africa and can be control using natural bioengineering methods.
Piet-Louis Grundling, who chairs the SA Wetland Society, believes it is a deliberate attempt to drain and degraded the area possibly for agricultural use. With the government spending R100 million a year to restore degraded wetlands, he questioned how a quarter of this amount could be used to drain a single wetland in the province. It seems the Department of Agriculture put up the cash.
WHY?
According to our main insider, application has been made to build a privately owned sugar cane biofuel refinery immediately adjacent to the Balamhlanga wetland...and he believes this land is being drained on purpose in preparation for sugar cane growing. (The wetland is on the periphery of the government-funded Mjindi irrigation scheme). I have the application. We will need to trace the owners and see if we can’t find any links to people at Ezemvelo. No EIA or approval from the Department of Water seems to exist. (National Water Act and the National Environmental Management Biodiversity Act say both of these approvals are needed for a project like this.)
Potential environmental disaster: Without this wetland to act as a filter from draining coming off all the surrounding farmlands...tons of nutrients will flood into the Pongola River and cause contamination. Not good! Think green slug and red alga flushes. And to top it all off this contaminated water will ultimately flood into the Pongola Wetland which is a RAMSAR site. (List of Wetlands of International Importance are Ramsar sites)
The SA Wetland Society called in the Green Scorpions. In a legal pre-compliance notice issued on June 15, the national Department of Environmental Affairs said there was reasonable ground to believe that the drainage was unlawful and had caused “significant environmental degradation” of the wetland, and the four parties could be held liable for several offences under national environmental and water protection laws.
The department said the damage was “exacerbated” by the apparent involvement of two government organs tasked with the protection of KZN’s natural resources, and also warned they could be held liable for criminal charges.
But 3 months later nothing appears to have been done....
• Battery Chicken Farming
And it seems the wetland fiasco isn’t the only project Ezemvelo is embroiled in involving agriculture. The organisation regency puts out a tender s worth R 5million to buy chicken broilers for a CSI project they are running on the borders of their parks.

Our insider says beside the ethical questions around a conservation agency being involved in intensive farming of animals, there is a solid argument to be made when it comes to the Biodiversity Act.

• Cattle Grazing in the parks

Last year the organisations head for the past 7 years – CEO Bandile Mkhize, gave permission to villagers live on the borders of Mskene Vlei (Another RANSAR Site) to graze their cattle in the park.

Buffalo in the park have mixed with the cattle and there is a fear the animals have cross contaminated each other with disease. The whole buffalo population now have to be culled.


• Building without EIA’s in its own parks

It seems Ezemvelo is guilty of flaunting its own processes...repeatedly. The agency recently completed a multimillion Rand lodge at Hlatikulu without doing an EIA. The Department of Environmental Affairs have slapped Ezemvelo with a notice to comply or tear down the building.

They also blew R 20 million doing up a camp site at Dedema for the MEC’s first lekothle...to which he never turned up.

• Parks in a shambles

Ezemvelo has been criticised for spending money on building new lodges when they can manage the ones they have.

I have a number of articles / letters to editors, where visitors to the various parks complain if dilapidated camps, shocking roads and dirty ablutions. Occupancy rates remain low and facilities and infrastructure are largely neglected. • Because of the inefficiency of the central reservations office, empty space in the game reserves is unused.

There have been suggestions that the running of facilities be put out to tender or a public-private partnership.
I have a tour operator who will take us to see all this. He says “If Ezemvelo was not subsidised it would have long gone out of business,” he said. “You need to look at how private game reserves operate and how to bring your occupancy rates up. You need to do more marketing.”

• Lack of skills

By its own admission, Ezemvelo has a serious skills shortage, many of its most competent officers having been drummed out of the organisation over the last few years. It has become so bad that some of the “old guard” that once drove the organisation have been recalled.

And while staff numbers had dropped by 193 in the last four years, the salary bill had gone up by R190 million

• Inflated salaries

While the number of visitors to its resorts and camp sites has been in decline, Ezemvelo’s salary bill has been increasing.

In 2013 the finance portfolio committee of the KwaZulu-Natal Legislature discovered that seventy percent of Ezemvelo KZN Wildlife’s R500 million budget was going on salaries and only 30% on service delivery.

And to top it all off ... last financial year R 40 million designated to service delivery was sent back to treasury unspent. Talk about people getting paid a fortune for not doing their jobs.

Then last year, the CEO and his merry band borrowed R 30 million from treasury and gave themselves all a massive salary hike. When the MEC of Environmental Affairs found out he demanded it all back ... staff protested in anger!


++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++
So what has happen in the past 10 years that has seen this once well run organisation slip so far?

On 4th September 2012, the High Court in Pietermaritzburg ruled that the Ezemvelo board was not validly appointed and has been operating illegally for nearly ten years. Without a validly appointed or constituted board, it seems Ezemvelo officials have been accountable to nobody. A law unto themselves it seems they have directed the organisation away from its statutory mandate and its core function.

The fact that only about 30% of its budget is spent on conservation activities says it all. Critics say it is no wonder that rhino poachers have the upper hand in KwaZulu-Natal! Our insider indicated that there are rumours that people working in the organisation are involved. BUT I don’t think we can go here without solid evidence. AND if we had it would be a story on its own...

• Wrong people for the job

CEO Bandile Mkhize – the inside joke is that the only way to get him to pitch up for work is to arrange a ribbon cutting. In fact I know the journalist that writes all his “columns” in the papers.

Apparently it his 2nd in command – Ntsike Dluwane that runs the show. Mkhize brought him with when he moved from Kruger (He used to be the Managing Executive of the Kruger National Park ). BUT Dluwane has zero conservation background. He ran a private business building low cost housing before this appointment. He’s seen as loose cannon by staff.

Ezemvelo has lost its focus. Instead of concentrating on its core function it has made itself extremely unpopular in just about every sector of society in which it operates, and in some cases, has no business to be:

Critics lament that the conservation of the province is not in safe hands

INTERVIEWS

We are going to have to hide the identities of the two insiders the story, for two reasons. 1. They have all had to sign a strange secrecy document that prevents them EVER talking about what goes on in the organisation. 2. They risk being axed. According to our main whistleblower the documents are legally questionable. The first one included segments from a military secrecy document. He will give us these docs to include as part of the story.

BUT through these people we can verify all the allegations. They will supply all supporting documentation too.


• Jeremy Riddle: Conservation Lawyer and very outspoken on the issue of Ezemvelo having lost focus and the bizarre goings on
• Someone from the Finance Portfolio Committee
• Piet-Louis Grundling, who chairs the SA Wetland Society
• Lal Jayamaha: International Tour operator fed up with conditions in the parks

Press Release:


Ezemvelo Investigated
The Natal Parks Board was once a well-respected wildlife entity synonymous with renowned conservationists like Dr Ian Player. Today, as Ezemvelo KZN Wildlife, it represents a symbol of gross mismanagement, with broken fences and parks in a serious state of neglect. Carte Blanche investigates.


Script:


EZEMVELO EXPOSED VIEWING SCRIPT
Ezemvelo KZN Wildlife, the old Natal Parks Board, was once a celebrated environmental agency, accredited with saving the southern white rhino from extinction under the watch of world renowned conservationist, Dr Ian Player.

Derek Sound Up: He’s been for a little mud bath.

Now they are allegedly plagued by chronic mismanagement, parks in a shambles and their reputation in tatters.

In July the Public Protector had to step in, when communities living alongside the Hluhluwe- Umfolozi Park near Ulundi, complained that they were being attacked by wild animals escaping through broken fences erected in the 1950s.

Ben Khanyile says his life changed forever when he was attacked by a leopard while looking after his live stock. He has been unable to work and support his family since.
Derek: Things are very difficult for you?
Ben: Angisenzi lutho manje nokudla angisakwazi ukudla ngiphiwa ilogogo.

SUBTITLE: I don’t do anything anymore. I can’t don’t even have food. I get it from this granny.
Local Councillor Misizwe Gcaba assisted in the Public Protector’s investigations. He took us
to the fences.

SOUND UP: Derek: “these poles are very fragile.”

Some have even rotted away.

LINK: I guess, this used to be a shiny steel cable but its days have long since
passed and this isn’t going to keep out anything, is it.? CUT HERE


We visited villages along the fence line, and found more victims.

Jabulani Shezi almost lost his finger to a leopard two years ago. And Ntombizethu Mkhize says a leopard attacked her while she was out collecting wood.

And according to Thuli Madonsela’s report livestock have become easy pickings with people having lost thousands of animals.

Dr Bandile Mkhize took over as Ezemvelo’s CEO in 2009. He didn’t seem fazed by the Public Protectors report.

Bandile: She is entitled to her views like any South African is entitled
Derek: But the families along the fence line are in danger.
Bandile: They are not in danger!

According to him attacks on humans are isolated and they have replaced some of the
123km fence that surrounds the park.

Bandile: Last year we did 12 kilometres.

And he says they are working with communities to reduce the risk to live stock, by
helping people build better kraals.

Bandile: Of course there will be problems here and there...but that doesn’t mean we are not doing our work.

But the 2013 auditor general’s report on Ezemvelo, tells a different story. R 44 million earmarked for maintenance and repairs went back to treasury unspent last year.

LINK: Now Ezemvelo under spent for maintenance and repairs on the fence by 24% last year.

Almost R 5million that could have been used to fix the fences.

The Public Protector laid the blame for the harm done at the door of the provincial Department of Environmental Affairs and Ezemvelo Wild Life, and accused them of failing to adequately compensate the victims of wild life attacks for their losses.

LINK: Now there are literally 2 sides to a fence in this condition. It lets the wild animals out as we can see, but it’s also a porous border that lets the poachers in.

85 rhino were poached from Ezemvelo parks last year.

Incredibly, Ezemvelo also sent back almost R 19 million they could have used for their Rhino Security Project, to treasury last year.

MEC for Environmenal Affairs in KZN, Mike Mabuyakhulu, who took over in May seems to be taking the fencing issue more seriously. He has set aside R 30 million to deal with the problem.

MEC: And that R30mill is going to be used – not only for fencing – but also to assist communities that are very close and adjacent to the game parks.

And it’s not just fencing that is isn’t being maintained. Visitors to some of Ezemvelo’s parks complain about dilapidated camp sites, and shocking roads.

LINK: Some visitors say that they spend more time looking for potholes than they do looking for game...and I can see or feel why....

According to the Auditor General, 87% of the budget for fixing and build roads also went
unspent.

Robert, a high ranking official at Ezemvelo, says it’s been a downhill slide since Bandile and
those he brought in, took charge. He asked us to hide his identity.

Rodger: Our procurement department is dysfunctional. They can’t work. They don’t do any work.

According to Ezemvelo, the auditor general never declared their procurement unit dysfunctional, and that gaps in the system have been corrected.

Still, the company contracted to fix the roads turned out not to have the capacity to do the job.

Bandile: And I’ve done everything a reasonable CEO will do. Because I put those people on terms and after I put them on terms then they started doing the work. And if you go there now –you will find them working.

We saw no sign of roadworks.

Environmental Lawyer, Jeremy Ridl, believes Ezemvelo is a government department that has run rogue.

Two years ago the Pietermaritzburg High Court found that Ezemvelo board was not properly constituted and has been operating unlawfully since 2003.

Jeremy: Historically, for a long time CEO’s of Ezemvelo have never been held accountable to
the board. And, therefore, until that is resolved until you have a board who calls the CEO
and holds him to account the problems are not going to go away.

Bandile: No. I disagree with that. We account for the decisions that we make.

But according to the Auditor General irregular expenditure has being going on for some time.

LINK: In 2012 the finance portfolio committee of the KZN Legislature discovered that 70% percent of the conservation agencies R500 million budget was spent on salaries and only 30% on service delivery.

More evidence says Jeremy that the organisation has lost focus of their core mandate to protect the environment.

This is used to be the Balamhlanga Natural Wetland near Jozini in the North East of the province. That’s until Ezemvelo allegedly drained it... at a cost of R 25 million.

Piet-Louis Grundling is an international wetlands expert.

Piet-Louis: Government is paying SANDBI, Working for Wetlands a R100 mill a
year to fix up wetlands and undo draining and here government spends R25million draining a priority wetland. Doesn’t make sense.

This footage of the damage on the ground was taken by Piet-Louis. On the right of the foot bridge is pristine wetland, as it used to be. On the left is where it’s been drained.

According to him they did this to make way for cattle grazing, using a herringbone drainage technique.

Piet-Louis. You can see the long straight canal, a drain down the middle and then all the side drains coming into it. It’s a very effective way of draining it if you have got a bit of a slope.

The wetland used to act as a natural filter, sifting out artificial nutrients in water that flowed through it from surrounding sugar cane farms.

Piet-Louis: All this water, nutrient rich water, is now ending up in the Pongola flood plain.

Piet-Louis says it is contaminating the river which supplies local towns and communities with water.

Jeremy insists that an Environmental Impact Assessment should have been done before
draining - but wasn’t.

Jeremy: Without that authorisation whoever under took that work was committing a
criminal offence.

Derek: What is a conservation agency draining a wetland you are supposed to protect?
Bandile: You know the history about this wetland?
Derek: Tell me
Bandile: You know we were doing this job on behalf of the Department of Agriculture and Environmental Affairs?
Derek: But surely as a department you work together and ensure that the environmental assessments have been done?
Bandile: We say to them, have you done all necessary things and they say yes we have done the necessary things...and that is how this happened!

Jeremy: It’s a bit rich for an organisation which is involved in environmental impact
assessments on a daily basis not to know and fully understand the law. And to say that they
assumed their sister department in agriculture has the necessary permission. That’s just not
believable.

We asked the KZN Department of Agriculture why they didn’t make sure an EIA was done.
They haven’t responded.

The National Department of Environmental Affairs are apparently deciding whether to
Charge those responsible at Ezemvelo criminally.

Jeremy: And the first in the firing line is going to be the CEO.

Meantime, Robert says staff morale is at an all time low.

In June workers went on strike citing unfair labour practises.

As part of a restructuring process started by Bandile, Staff alleged that a handful of top executives were given irregular salary hikes.

Robert: Two thirds of the money for the restructuring was spent on these huge salaries and staff were saying, ‘Well what’s happening to us?” Then it started coming out that there were insufficient funds to do the whole lot.

Derek: Your executives salaries have sky rocketed and most of the workers
are getting a pittance. And that’s why they went on strike?
Bandile: And that’s a question I am not going to answer because I have already said
to you the MEC’s task team is dealing with that.

MEC Mabuyakhulu has taken a tough stance. He has deployed a task team to investigate and has ordered the executives to pay back their supposedly exorbitant salary increases.

MEC: They have to pay back the money. So that directive has been given and now it is being implemented.

Some assets unfortunately can’t be returned.

When Zulu King Goodwill Zwelethini married his 6th wife in July this year – Ezemvelo
provided the meat.

LINK: On the menu warthog, buffalo and a giraffe!

Bandile: We have off takes every year, approved by our board. And on the basis of that we give some of the animals to the king.

Jeremy: Where is Ezemvelo justified that taking animals which belong to the public and
Appropriating those to private use, even if its private use by the royal family.

The Kings spokesperson and head sangoma, Mr DH Nyawo defended the acquisition saying
that the animal’s organs were used for customary rituals that benefit all the people of KZN.

Mr Nyawo: To protect the nature and to protect ourselves.

Jeremy says not all is lost; there is a new board which Bandile will have to answer to and an MEC who is promising to sweep clean.

MEC: Where anyone has acted outside of conduct, proper conduct, and the decision for us

It is section 24(1) of the National Environmental Management Act 107 of 1998 (NEMA) that requires environmental authorisation for any "listed activity". It is an offence under section 24F to undertake the activity. If an activity has commenced without environmental authorisation, it can be rectified under section 24G. This involves the prior payment of a hefty fine. The "listed activities" are published in Listing Notices - 1, 2 and 3. Digging up a wetland would be Listed Activity 18 which is the depositing into or excavation of more than 5 cubic metres from a watercourse (which includes wetlands). If more than 50 square metres of infrastructure is to be built in or within 32 metres from the edge of the watercourse/wetland, it needs environmental authorisation. To get environmental authorisation, you need to follow the Basic Assessment process. This is a lesser version of the EIA process. Activities in Listing Notice 2 require a full Scoping and EIA process. Listing Notice 3 covers activities in or within 5 km of protected areas and 10km of World Heritage Sites. Included in these lists is the removal of more than 300 square metres of endangered vegetation or more than 1 hectare of indigenous vegetation. A water use licence for the activities would also be needed and the procedure to obtain a licence is the same as a conventional EIA.

metadata.One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...): Accused of destroying wetlands, building illegally in conservation areas and blowing 70% of its budget on ridiculous salaries, Ezemvelo ZN Wildlife is accused of doing more harm than good.
metadata.Summary: Formerly known as the Natal Parks Board, the organisation was once a celebrated environmental agency accredited with saving the white rhino from extinction. Areas of operation include the world’s biggest marine turtle breeding beaches, Coelacanth habitat and 2 world heritage sites. But, according to high ranking insiders, the organisation is now chronically mismanaged with its parks in a shambles and its reputation in tatters.
metadata.Further information: TTHE STORY There are a number of cases of questionable and bizarre projects that see Ezemvelo going against its own mandate to protect the environment and conserve nature. We will start with the most visually shocking – the destruction of the unauthorised” drainage of large section of the Balamhlanga natural wetland in the Makhatini Flats near Jozini. VISUALS: I’m going to take the presenter up and let them see it firsthand. We’ll open with this sequence. • Balamhlanga Natural Wetland Ezemvelo is currently helping to rip up and drain a large natural wetland near Jozini at a cost of R25 million. Conservationists and wetland experts want to know why the provincial conservation agency is helping to destroy a specially protected natural wetland. At first Ezemvelo and the Department of Agriculture and Environmental Affairs said they were just trying to get rid of a “weed invasion”. However, wetland experts have confirmed that the bulrushes at Balamhlanga are not alien, but indigenous to South Africa and can be control using natural bioengineering methods. Piet-Louis Grundling, who chairs the SA Wetland Society, believes it is a deliberate attempt to drain and degraded the area possibly for agricultural use. With the government spending R100 million a year to restore degraded wetlands, he questioned how a quarter of this amount could be used to drain a single wetland in the province. It seems the Department of Agriculture put up the cash. WHY? According to our main insider, application has been made to build a privately owned sugar cane biofuel refinery immediately adjacent to the Balamhlanga wetland...and he believes this land is being drained on purpose in preparation for sugar cane growing. (The wetland is on the periphery of the government-funded Mjindi irrigation scheme). I have the application. We will need to trace the owners and see if we can’t find any links to people at Ezemvelo. No EIA or approval from the Department of Water seems to exist. (National Water Act and the National Environmental Management Biodiversity Act say both of these approvals are needed for a project like this.) Potential environmental disaster: Without this wetland to act as a filter from draining coming off all the surrounding farmlands...tons of nutrients will flood into the Pongola River and cause contamination. Not good! Think green slug and red alga flushes. And to top it all off this contaminated water will ultimately flood into the Pongola Wetland which is a RAMSAR site. (List of Wetlands of International Importance are Ramsar sites) The SA Wetland Society called in the Green Scorpions. In a legal pre-compliance notice issued on June 15, the national Department of Environmental Affairs said there was reasonable ground to believe that the drainage was unlawful and had caused “significant environmental degradation” of the wetland, and the four parties could be held liable for several offences under national environmental and water protection laws. The department said the damage was “exacerbated” by the apparent involvement of two government organs tasked with the protection of KZN’s natural resources, and also warned they could be held liable for criminal charges. But 3 months later nothing appears to have been done.... • Battery Chicken Farming And it seems the wetland fiasco isn’t the only project Ezemvelo is embroiled in involving agriculture. The organisation regency puts out a tender s worth R 5million to buy chicken broilers for a CSI project they are running on the borders of their parks. Our insider says beside the ethical questions around a conservation agency being involved in intensive farming of animals, there is a solid argument to be made when it comes to the Biodiversity Act. • Cattle Grazing in the parks Last year the organisations head for the past 7 years – CEO Bandile Mkhize, gave permission to villagers live on the borders of Mskene Vlei (Another RANSAR Site) to graze their cattle in the park. Buffalo in the park have mixed with the cattle and there is a fear the animals have cross contaminated each other with disease. The whole buffalo population now have to be culled. • Building without EIA’s in its own parks It seems Ezemvelo is guilty of flaunting its own processes...repeatedly. The agency recently completed a multimillion Rand lodge at Hlatikulu without doing an EIA. The Department of Environmental Affairs have slapped Ezemvelo with a notice to comply or tear down the building. They also blew R 20 million doing up a camp site at Dedema for the MEC’s first lekothle...to which he never turned up. • Parks in a shambles Ezemvelo has been criticised for spending money on building new lodges when they can manage the ones they have. I have a number of articles / letters to editors, where visitors to the various parks complain if dilapidated camps, shocking roads and dirty ablutions. Occupancy rates remain low and facilities and infrastructure are largely neglected. • Because of the inefficiency of the central reservations office, empty space in the game reserves is unused. There have been suggestions that the running of facilities be put out to tender or a public-private partnership. I have a tour operator who will take us to see all this. He says “If Ezemvelo was not subsidised it would have long gone out of business,” he said. “You need to look at how private game reserves operate and how to bring your occupancy rates up. You need to do more marketing.” • Lack of skills By its own admission, Ezemvelo has a serious skills shortage, many of its most competent officers having been drummed out of the organisation over the last few years. It has become so bad that some of the “old guard” that once drove the organisation have been recalled. And while staff numbers had dropped by 193 in the last four years, the salary bill had gone up by R190 million • Inflated salaries While the number of visitors to its resorts and camp sites has been in decline, Ezemvelo’s salary bill has been increasing. In 2013 the finance portfolio committee of the KwaZulu-Natal Legislature discovered that seventy percent of Ezemvelo KZN Wildlife’s R500 million budget was going on salaries and only 30% on service delivery. And to top it all off ... last financial year R 40 million designated to service delivery was sent back to treasury unspent. Talk about people getting paid a fortune for not doing their jobs. Then last year, the CEO and his merry band borrowed R 30 million from treasury and gave themselves all a massive salary hike. When the MEC of Environmental Affairs found out he demanded it all back ... staff protested in anger! ++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++ So what has happen in the past 10 years that has seen this once well run organisation slip so far? On 4th September 2012, the High Court in Pietermaritzburg ruled that the Ezemvelo board was not validly appointed and has been operating illegally for nearly ten years. Without a validly appointed or constituted board, it seems Ezemvelo officials have been accountable to nobody. A law unto themselves it seems they have directed the organisation away from its statutory mandate and its core function. The fact that only about 30% of its budget is spent on conservation activities says it all. Critics say it is no wonder that rhino poachers have the upper hand in KwaZulu-Natal! Our insider indicated that there are rumours that people working in the organisation are involved. BUT I don’t think we can go here without solid evidence. AND if we had it would be a story on its own... • Wrong people for the job CEO Bandile Mkhize – the inside joke is that the only way to get him to pitch up for work is to arrange a ribbon cutting. In fact I know the journalist that writes all his “columns” in the papers. Apparently it his 2nd in command – Ntsike Dluwane that runs the show. Mkhize brought him with when he moved from Kruger (He used to be the Managing Executive of the Kruger National Park ). BUT Dluwane has zero conservation background. He ran a private business building low cost housing before this appointment. He’s seen as loose cannon by staff. Ezemvelo has lost its focus. Instead of concentrating on its core function it has made itself extremely unpopular in just about every sector of society in which it operates, and in some cases, has no business to be: Critics lament that the conservation of the province is not in safe hands INTERVIEWS We are going to have to hide the identities of the two insiders the story, for two reasons. 1. They have all had to sign a strange secrecy document that prevents them EVER talking about what goes on in the organisation. 2. They risk being axed. According to our main whistleblower the documents are legally questionable. The first one included segments from a military secrecy document. He will give us these docs to include as part of the story. BUT through these people we can verify all the allegations. They will supply all supporting documentation too. • Jeremy Riddle: Conservation Lawyer and very outspoken on the issue of Ezemvelo having lost focus and the bizarre goings on • Someone from the Finance Portfolio Committee • Piet-Louis Grundling, who chairs the SA Wetland Society • Lal Jayamaha: International Tour operator fed up with conditions in the parks
